findings.title: Third-party advertising SDK receiving user identifiers

dpdp_ref.explanation: Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional, unambiguous with clear affirmative action, and limited to necessary personal data.

findings.justification: Risk Score 64/125: Sensitivity (4/5 - email, phone, device_id) x Exposure (4/5 - transferred) x Exploit (4/5). Evaluated against DPDP Act 2023 impact thresholds.
findings.fix: Gate advertising tracker scripts behind verified consent gating (Rule 3/4).

findings.title: Insecure plaintext HTTP endpoint configured for data transfer

dpdp_ref.explanation: Specifies technical standards: end-to-end encryption in transit (TLS 1.3), encryption at rest (AES-256), cryptographic key lifecycle, access auditing, and secure containerization.

findings.justification: Risk Score 80/125: Sensitivity (5/5 - email, phone, aadhaar, pan, financial) x Exposure (4/5 - transferred) x Exploit (4/5). Evaluated against DPDP Act 2023 impact thresholds.
findings.fix: Enforce TLS 1.3 by updating endpoint URIs from http:// to https://.

checks.name: Consent Recordation & Provenance
checks.description: Verifies that consent logs capture timestamp, purpose identifier, and active privacy notice version.
checks.recommendation: Store an immutable consent audit record containing { userId, purposeId, noticeVersion, timestamp, ipAddress } on every grant.
checks.evidence: No structured consent provenance schema found.

checks.name: Ease of Consent Withdrawal (Section 6(4))
checks.description: Ensures Data Principals have automated endpoints and UI controls to revoke consent as easily as it was given.
checks.recommendation: Expose DELETE /api/consent or POST /api/consent/withdraw with cascading signals to downstream processors.
checks.evidence: No dedicated consent revocation endpoints found.

checks.name: Backend Pre-Processing Consent Enforcement
checks.description: Checks whether backend middleware gates personal data processing against active consent state before execution.
checks.recommendation: Implement a requireConsent(purpose) middleware to block processing if the Data Principal has not opted in.
checks.evidence: No backend consent verification middleware detected.

checks.name: Granular Purpose Separation (Section 6(1))
checks.description: Verifies that consent requests are split per discrete processing purpose rather than bundled into an all-or-nothing checkbox.
checks.recommendation: Separate consent toggles by discrete purpose (Essential, Analytics, Marketing, Third-party Sharing).
checks.evidence: Single bundled or binary consent model detected.

checks.name: Plain Language Itemised Notice (Section 5 & Rule 3)
checks.description: Checks for accessible privacy notices specifying personal data items, specific purposes, and Grievance Officer details.
checks.recommendation: Publish an itemised privacy notice in clear language with contact info of the Data Protection Officer.
checks.evidence: No accessible privacy notice with statutory disclosures found.

third_party_egress.description: Meta Pixel tracking user pageviews, actions, and identities without prior itemised consent.
third_party_egress.remediation: Gate 'Meta / Facebook Pixel' call behind verified user consent: `if (hasConsent('Advertising & Tracking')) { ... }`

third_party_egress.description: Meta Pixel tracking user pageviews, actions, and identities without prior itemised consent.
third_party_egress.remediation: Gate 'Meta / Facebook Pixel' call behind verified user consent: `if (hasConsent('Advertising & Tracking')) { ... }`

third_party_egress.description: Outbound HTTP egress transmitting customer data to external hosts over unencrypted plaintext HTTP.
third_party_egress.remediation: Gate 'Insecure Third-Party Webhook / HTTP Endpoint' call behind verified user consent: `if (hasConsent('Data Egress')) { ... }`

malfunctions.title: Silent Exception Swallowing / Empty Catch Block
malfunctions.description: Empty catch block silently suppresses runtime errors, causing unexpected application halts and data inconsistencies.
malfunctions.fix: Log the caught exception using a structured logger or rethrow with proper context.
